title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises

We had the best experience ever, aboard Cape Adieu!

Online booking through the website was a piece of cake.

We were met by Munro at the gate which was a nice surprise. Once checked off, we were shown to our seats and our first drinks order was taken. All night the staff were attentive and saw to our every need.

The food was sensational - all delish, but the yam puree with the steak was incredible!

Munro gave us (and all passengers) plenty of his time, telling stories about the boat and his time in agriculture before taking over the business. He even took some great photos of our group and the setting sun, which he kindly shared following our trip.

All round - this cruise was brilliant and a must do if you're in Darwin! Not sure when we'll be back in the NT, but if we are, we'll be sure to sail again!

title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises
text:
Now, for transparency I have to say that I'm not a fan of seafood. So, why did I get the sunset cruise and dine experience then?
Well m'hearties, my wife loves seafood and if I didn't say yes then my timbers would have been shivered and mainbrace well and truely spliced.
Sitting on the top deck gave a great view of the harbour and access to much needed breeze. After a long day in the tropical sun, I was a tad on the nose.
Roberto, not to be confused with Robert downstairs, was helpful and attentive, and efficiently helped as the cruise progressed.
Not doing seafood well I asked my wife for entree feedback. Oysters - fresh as ( well no replay as of yet), prawns were nice, and even I tried the smoked mackerel ( my guess is Spanish type rather than the little tin types). It was very nice.
To get into the swing, I went for the Jewfish main (you can have steak if you so desire instead). Again, cooked on board on hot flat grill - and help yourself salad.
All of it was nice.
I've seen reviews saying there wasn't enough, but, it wasn't an issue for us. Perhaps, some context or reality checks by those reviewers, but that's their thoughts so onwards and upwards.
Nicely sunburnt and crispy as the sunsets, gave an opportunity to David Bailey up, and phones a plenty were out - probably with many fingers and thumbs taking centre stage.
I didn't go the fruit salad for dessert but again, just by sight ( having a quick butchers around other tables) there was plenty to go around.
You could take your own drinks, but there was a list of beers, wines and soft drinks at bar prices. If you've splurged on the cruise make it an adventure and buy some house drinkies.
I'm sure Grace (hostess) gets fed up running up and down the steep stairs, but she's a natural at this hospitality business.
Any gripes? My wife wouldn't tell me how much it was, so probs not cheap; I couldn't hear the music, or more importantly the capitano spiel as I think a speaker had died.
Look it was a treat of sorts, and so any cost must reflect that (apparently it was about $150 ea).
It is also run out of Darwin Harbour in the top end. There's no place for Italian loafers (Roberto worked hard) or channel no 5.
There are other cruises run in purpose designed vessels, but this had history, and the cruises are now part of it. So, steep steps and low walkways aside, give it a go. Treat a special one, and you may get more than just memories on your return.

title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises
text:
A nice evening. Calm waters, no wind and a great on-board atmosphere. Recommended. The new owners are making a good go of it, their enthusiasm is evident. At $155 per person can we say there was value for money. Probably yes with a few changes to the food offering. Staff were excellent and couldn’t be faulted.
Entree was buffet style 3 types of seafood - beautiful Coffin Bay oysters that were so fresh you could still taste the sea. Prawns in their shell and smoked fish which was also very good. Diners were asked up by table and considering the limited space this was a good idea.
Mains were steak and fish. I asked for a rare steak and was very happy with it. Rare was the way to go as the steaks were on the thin side but a good size. Both dishes were presented with no garnish. Salads were available at the buffet. First suggestion, a salad bowl served to the table would be more appreciated rather than stand in a cue, steak in hand, waiting for space at the salad bar. Extra plates in a small kitchen but worth the added comfort factor for diners.
Then there was dessert. The biggest disappointment of the night. Cut up fruit at said buffet!  Very reminiscent of a day trip to the reef including lunch. Individual cheesecakes or something similar served to table would have been better appreciated. And seriously, for $155 per head, would have been more in keeping with expectation.
The boat was licensed and the limited selection was fine and bottle prices $40 to $45. Sensible pricing for dinner on board.
The night was successful and we congratulate the new owners, an enthusiastic couple with a vision. With a few little tweaks, the evening’s experience would have been much improved.

title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises
text:
I organised my engagement party with these guys and it was absolutely fantastic. We had friends and family come up from down south and they were extremely impressed.
Matthew was the main person I corresponded with, and he was always extremely helpful, accommodating and punctual with replying to my many questions.
The food was brilliant as well, the chef seemed a bit young when I first saw him, but he definitely knows what he is doing, every course was amazing.
The other staff and the captain of the boat were just as fantastic as the others, really helpful and happy to answer questions, bring drinks over to people (we brought all our own drinks) and even help out the younger members of our entourage; my little brother had trouble with his steak and without a word from anyone, one of the staff members was cutting up his steak for him.

The night was absolutely fantastic and I cannot fault these guys on anything, thank you so much for such a memorable night!

title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises
text: The cruise was very informative and the sunset was lovely.However I don't think the buffet meal was value for money. Only 4 salads, one being tinned baby beets and another couscous.  The other two were nice but they ran out by the time the main course cane round. Only one dessert which was a small crumble which I liked but it would have been nice to have a choice. $92 for seniors not worth the money

title: Cape Adieu Harbour Cruises
text: My sister and her husband were visiting Darwin and we took them out on a sunset cruise on the Cape Adieu. It was the most wonderful night - we were seated on the top deck at the stern and had a wonderful view, delicious food and excellent music interspersed with informative commentary about the sights we sailed past. The weather was perfect and the crew were organised and attentive. This was the best outing we have ever had in our 2 years in Darwin. We will take all our visitors on this cruise in future.
